text:
Richard Stallman was born on March 16, 1953, in New York City. His early interest in computers stemmed from reading manuals for the IBM 7094 at a summer camp. In 1970, he worked at the IBM New York Scientific Center, where he wrote numerical analysis programs and text editors. He later became a programmer at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, where he was known as RMS and received a bachelor's degree in physics from Harvard in 1974.
Stallman became an ardent critic of restricted computer access, notably decrypting passwords in 1977. This growing opposition to proprietary software, which began fragmenting the hacker culture in the late 1970s and early 1980s due to copyright and restrictive licenses, led to his founding of the GNU project in September 1983. He published the GNU Manifesto in 1985, outlining his motivation for creating a free operating system compatible with Unix. Stallman popularized the concept of copyleft, implemented in the GNU Emacs General Public License, and founded the Free Software Foundation in 1985 to support the free software movement.
